_meta.indication: LASTACAFT is an H1 histamine receptor antagonist indicated for the prevention of itching associated with allergic conjunctivitis.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-masked, randomized, vehicle-controlled conjunctival allergen challenge (CAC) trial; subjects assigned to alcaftadine bilaterally, alcaftadine in one eye and vehicle in the fellow eye, or vehicle bilaterally.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 10 years of age or older with a history of allergic conjunctivitis or allergic rhinoconjunctivitis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of ocular itching and conjunctival redness, each scored 0 to 4; itching evaluated by subjects at 3, 5, and 7 minutes post allergen challenge.
pivotal_trials.result: Alcaftadine produced approximately one unit or greater improvement in ocular itching score versus vehicle at all post-challenge time points; p<0.001. The co-primary conjunctival redness endpoint was not met.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-center, randomized, double-masked, vehicle (placebo)-controlled study using the CAC model.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 10 years of age or older with a history of allergic conjunctivitis or allergic rhinoconjunctivitis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of ocular itching and conjunctival redness (0 to 4 scale).
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in ocular itching versus vehicle (p<0.001 at all post-challenge time points); redness endpoint not met.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-masked, randomized, vehicle-controlled CAC study; subjects assigned to receive alcaftadine or vehicle bilaterally.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 10 years of age or older with a history of allergic conjunctivitis or allergic rhinoconjunctivitis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of ocular itching and conjunctival redness (0 to 4 scale).
pivotal_trials.result: Successful for ocular itching endpoint (p<0.001 at all post-challenge time points); failed for ocular redness.

nct_ctgov.title: Safety and Efficacy Study of a Eye Drop for Eye Allergy

key_safety: Most common ocular adverse reactions (<4% of treated eyes): eye irritation, burning and/or stinging on instillation, eye redness, and eye pruritus. Most common non-ocular adverse reactions (<3% of subjects): nasopharyngitis, headache and influenza.
target_moa: Alcaftadine is a topically active, direct H1-receptor antagonist and an inhibitor of the release of histamine from mast cells.

rems.type: There are no proposed risk management actions except the usual post-marketing collection and reporting of adverse experiences associated with the use of drug product.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because there are other approved ophthalmic products in this class with this indication and the safety/efficacy data posed no particular concerns.

description.text: Full prescription-to-over-the-counter (Rx-to-OTC) switch of Lastacraft (alcaftadine ophthalmic solution), 0.25%

citations.quote: This "Prior Approval" supplemental new drug application provides for the full prescription-to-over-the-counter (Rx-to-OTC) switch of Lastacraft (alcaftadine ophthalmic solution), 0.25%.

summary.text: Standard-review NDA submitted under section 505(b), approved first cycle based on three Phase 3 conjunctival allergen challenge efficacy studies demonstrating prevention of ocular itching; no advisory committee, no REMS, and no Phase 4 commitments.

citations.quote: The Phase 3 clinical development program to support the NDA filing is comprised of a 6-week safety study (05-003-10) and three efficacy CAC studies (05-003-11, 05-003-13, and 09-003-05). The numbers of subjects enrolled in these studies were 909, 126, 88, and 60, respectively.
received September 29, 2009, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Lastacraft (alcaftadine ophthalmic solution) 0.25%.
There are no recommended Phase 4 clinical study commitments.
